basis: Rib/scapular anomalies and cleft palate define the syndrome; Pierre Robin sequence includes glossoptosis with persistent upper-airway obstruction.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: upper-airway obstruction from glossoptosis is a defining component of Pierre Robin sequence; airways belong to this axis.

basis: Chronic peripheral nerve damage; metabolic causation does not establish a separate intrinsic metabolic or endocrine disorder within this concept.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: this concept describes neuropathy attributed to metabolic causes, rather than a defined disorder of metabolism or an endocrine gland.

basis: Cerebellar/brainstem malformation and developmental impairment define disease. Ocular motor findings are central; retinal damage frequency is unknown. Renal insufficiency is 2/13.

decisions.ocular: none: nystagmus and esotropia (5/13) reflect central oculomotor dysfunction; direct retinal or other ocular damage is not established in >=30%.

basis: Pediatric Castleman disease is predominantly unicentric lymphoid proliferation; infection or immune-mediated disease is not established across this umbrella.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: predominantly unicentric pediatric disease is not necessarily infectious, autoimmune or immune-mediated; lymphoid proliferation alone does not qualify.

basis: Desmin-related skeletal myopathy with defining cardiomyopathy and conduction disease, supported by cardiac HPO frequencies of 30-79%. Respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiomyopathy and conduction disease are defining manifestations in the definition and cardiomyopathy ancestry, with frequent cardiac HPO findings.

basis: Retinal dystrophy, obesity/hypogonadism and developmental delay define disease. Polydactyly occurs in 8/8 and is a major criterion; renal dysplasia is only 5-29%.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment is a defining feature and global developmental delay occurs in 8/8; prioritized within the three-primary cap.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: polydactyly occurs in 8/8 and is a major diagnostic criterion; retained as the fourth axis after prioritizing visual, endocrine and neurologic disease.

basis: Lysosomal storage encephalopathy. Hepatosplenomegaly in 2/2 does not establish functional organ damage; respiratory insufficiency lacks direct lung evidence; optic atrophy is 5-29%.

decisions.haematologic: none: splenomegaly in 2/2 establishes enlargement, but no hypersplenism, cytopenia or other splenic functional impairment is documented.
decisions.hepatic: none: hepatomegaly in 2/2 without demonstrated hepatic dysfunction or fibrosis does not establish function-impairing storage.

basis: Splenoportal venous malformation defines disease. Hepatic fibrosis/cirrhosis are reported without frequencies establishing >=30% or major diagnostic status; splenomegaly alone is insufficient.

decisions.hepatic: none: fibrosis and cirrhosis establish possible hepatic damage, but the supplied evidence does not establish their frequency or status as defining criteria.

basis: Hereditary axonal sensorimotor neuropathy; muscle wasting and foot deformities follow denervation rather than direct skeletal disease. Cardiomyopathy frequency is unestablished.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: distal amyotrophy and foot deformities are consequences of motor denervation; direct disease of muscle, bone or joints is not established.

basis: Distal 7p deletion commonly causes developmental impairment; skeletal abnormalities vary with deletion extent and are not established as defining across the umbrella or present in >=30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: craniosynostosis and other skeletal defects depend on deletion extent; the evidence does not establish a qualifying frequency across distal 7p deletions.
